items.text: The Iranian national beach soccer team secured first place in Group B of the 2026 Asian Beach Soccer Championship by defeating Lebanon 7-2 and advanced to the next stage with their third consecutive win. Mohahed Mohammadpour, Mohammad Masoumi-Zadeh, and Mohammad Ali Mokhtari each scored twice, and Seyed Mehdi Mirjalili scored another goal. Iran had already secured advancement by winning against Afghanistan and Vietnam.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, called the condemnation of the Islamic Republic's actions by Germany and Qatar "rejected and unacceptable" and said Qatar's statements were "unexpected". He also announced the summoning of Qatar's chargé d'affaires to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the delivery of the Islamic Republic's protest. Baqaei said about the Qatari Prime Minister's trip to Washington that stopping the war on all fronts is an integral part of any agreement and this demand shows the Islamic Republic's responsibility for regional security and stability.
Fatemeh (Hasti) Varamziar, a citizen from Ilam, was arrested on Sunday, 1 Azar, after being summoned and referring to the prosecutor's office of this city and was transferred to Ilam prison.

Pirhossein Kolivand, head of the Red Crescent, said that during the California wildfires he sent a letter to the US offering to send forces to help. He added that the Americans responded that they did not need forces and asked for financial assistance instead.

Amin Soltani, former board member of Esteghlal Khuzestan club, confirmed that inappropriate messages were exchanged between a youth team coach and several players. He said that the documents of this case were submitted to supervisory bodies and the authenticity of the messages was confirmed by these bodies. Soltani added that efforts were made for the coach to resign, but this did not happen and the issue escalated.

Israeli media reported that Israeli military intelligence agencies have warned Benjamin Netanyahu that a unilateral attack on the Islamic Republic could lead to the expansion of the war to Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza. Channels 11 and 12 and the Walla website reported that the White House prefers to wait at least another week to assess the impact of the siege.

Fatemeh Manouchehri, a national para-athletics athlete and bronze medalist at the Asian and Oceania Championships, died on Tuesday, 2 Azar, after about a month in a coma. Fars News Agency reported that the cause of her coma was cardiac arrest. Manouchehri competed in shot put and placed sixth in this event at the Hangzhou Para Asian Games in China.

On Monday, 2 Azar, a group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in the cities of Kermanshah and Sanandaj. The retirees demanded the implementation of regulation 89/24, enforcement of Administrative Justice Court ruling 9235, salary adjustments, and attention to their other demands.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said the US does not have the capability for a ground attack on the Islamic Republic and that a naval attack would involve significant risks and costs. He added that the only military option available to the US is airstrikes, which would be met with reciprocal responses. Naqdi also said US politicians hope economic pressures will cause public despair and weaken officials' resolve, but officials and military forces will not retreat under these pressures.

According to information received by Iran International, the family of Alireza Raeisi, an executed protester, was forced by security agents to cover the poem engraved on his tombstone in the deserts of Anarak in Isfahan province with black spray. The poem on his tombstone praised those who left the world with dignity and embraced truth. Alireza Raeisi, one of the detainees in the so-called "Alikhani Square" case in Isfahan, was executed on 13 Mehr.

Student councils of 31 universities in the country issued a joint statement declaring they will not remain silent against "fabrication of cases" and disciplinary actions against student representatives. The statement mentioned the issuance of a four-semester suspension for Pejman Nasiri and called for the cancellation of this sentence and the guarantee of the independence of student councils. Reports of case formations and pressure on council members at various universities have also been received.

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona star, will miss Wednesday night's match against Sabah in the UEFA Champions League due to a minor discomfort in his right ankle. The club announced that he will not participate in this game as a precaution and is expected to return next Sunday against Deportivo La Coruña. Yamal played the full 90 minutes in the previous match but the medical staff decided not to field him in the upcoming game to prevent worsening the issue.

Lida Pirasteh, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Semnan, was summoned and interrogated by the Intelligence Department of this city for the second time. This Bahá'í citizen was also summoned and interrogated by this security agency yesterday. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said at an event that the US and Europe cannot overthrow us unless we overthrow ourselves. He emphasized the need for interaction and kindness in conversations and added that if God's and the Imam's orders are followed, all problems will be solved.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial board, referred to statements by Mostafa Izadi, deputy commander of the IRGC, about the readiness of the IRGC and Basij to confront internal unrest. He said the Islamic Republic's main concern is the return of widespread protests to the streets. He considered the claim of about 450,000 Basij members participating in Tehran IRGC programs exaggerated and said the government tries to intimidate people before new protests by announcing such figures and repeated threats.

The strike of truck drivers and drivers in several cities in Iran entered its second day on Monday, 2 Azar, amid the intensification of the fuel crisis and worsening economic conditions. The Union of Truck Drivers' Associations announced that the strike will continue until the drivers' demands are met, and Nissan drivers have also joined the strike.

A two-day meeting of Afghan women hosted by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs began on Sunday, 1 Azar, in Madrid. At the same time, the campaign "One Million Voices for Afghan Women and Girls" has called for concrete action by the international community to secure women's rights.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing widespread power outages on Sunday, the first of Azar, and said they have no electricity and all people are living under pressure, but they do not lose hope.

The Iranian women's national handball team defeated Hong Kong 33-16 in their first match at the Asian Championship hosted by Kazakhstan. Fatemeh Khalili, the goalkeeper of the Iranian national team, was named the best player on the field. Iran is in Group A with Japan, China, Thailand, and Hong Kong, and will face China tomorrow, November 24, at 15:30.

Bild newspaper reported that about 450 schools across Germany received bomb threat emails on Monday morning. German police stated that these messages with identical text were sent to hundreds of schools and investigations have started to identify the senders. Police said the threats are not currently considered serious and a case has been opened on charges of "disturbing public order through threats of committing a crime."

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said on Tuesday, 2 Azar, that the Islamic Republic is "not susceptible to siege." He added: "We will take any action to break the siege."

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic summoned the Qatari chargé d'affaires in the absence of the country's ambassador in protest against the joint statement by Qatar and Germany against the Islamic Republic. Esmail Baghayi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, called Qatar's position on the nuclear file and maritime security "surprising and regrettable." Qatar and Germany condemned missile attacks and threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in their joint statement.

Shahrouz Sadidi, a resident of Sabzevar, remains in detention without a clear status despite 55 days passing since his arrest. He was previously held in quarantine ward and has now been transferred to the general ward. Judicial officials have not provided a clear explanation regarding the handling of his case, and his lawyers have not been able to access his file.
A second-grade student in the village of Siyahkaleh in Dorud county says in a video that the Molavi school teacher in this village broke his foot because he did not write his homework.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, responded to criticisms of corruption among government officials by saying those who make such claims should closely observe the lives of these individuals. He added that some of those who were killed had simple lives and even one of the commanders did not have a house of his own.

Videos received show that retirees in Kermanshah, Isfahan, and Sanandaj came to the streets on Tuesday, 2 Azar, to demand their rights and called the "Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order Headquarters" and the "Cooperative Foundation of the IRGC" "usurpers."

Amnesty International has issued a public call for protesters, families of the killed, eyewitnesses, healthcare workers, and others with information about the January 2026 protests to participate in documenting these events. Amnesty stated that many aspects of the January killings still need precise documentation and that recording "patterns of killing and injuring protesters" is important for increasing global attention and enabling judicial prosecution of Islamic Republic officials. The call especially asks those with information about the events of January 9 and 10 in Tehran, Isfahan, Rasht, Mashhad, and Shiraz to contact the organization via secure messengers, assuring confidentiality of sources and contacts.

Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher living in Nurabad Mamasani, has been detained in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz for over eight months. His legal case was recently transferred from Branch 10 of Shiraz Prosecutor's Office to Branch 2 of Nurabad Mamasani Prosecutor's Office. According to Harana News Agency, Ali Ahmadi remains in detention.

Mostafa Nili, a lawyer, announced that the sentence of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi and four others involved in the so-called "hypothetical concert" at the historic Dirgachin Caravanserai in Qom has been carried out. After the sentence was finalized and the case sent to enforcement, these individuals appeared at the Qom prosecutor's office and the lash punishment was executed. The sentence was issued on charges of "violating public decency through producing and publishing obscene and immoral content in cyberspace."

Ukraine released new images of its naval drones attacking a Russian warship and sinking it in the port of Benghazi, Libya. This operation has been described as one of the most important attacks during the Ukraine war.

The ceremony marking the 28th anniversary of the murder of Dariush and Parvaneh Forouhar was held on Sunday evening under threats from security and judicial institutions at the Forouhar family residence in Tehran. Morteza Kazemian explains the case of the political murders in autumn 1377 and the brutal killing of the Forouhars, and speaks about the continuation of intimidation by the Islamic Republic, suppression of opponents in Iran, and the deepening divide between the nation and the government.

A source familiar with the situation of Bahá'í citizens in Iran told Iran International that Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested Kimia Mostafavi, Roha Imani, and Hooman Imani, three Bahá'í citizens, in Kerman and summoned Leida Pirasteh, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Semnan, for the second consecutive day to the Intelligence Department. Mostafavi and Roha Imani were arrested on the night of Sunday, 1 Azar, and Hooman Imani on the morning of Monday, 2 Azar. After searching their homes and confiscating personal belongings, agents transferred them to an unknown location.

Slogan writing is an important part of the protests that have intensified in Iran these days. Videos received by Iran International show the writing of the slogan "Long live the Shah" on the walls of public passages in the city of Rasht.

It was announced by Shams Azar Qazvin club that Voria Ghafouri, former captain of Esteghlal, was appointed as the new head coach of the club. Ghafouri replaces Vahid Rezaei, who was dismissed from coaching on the first of Azar. Shams Azar has had poor results in the current season of the Iranian Premier League and is currently in seventeenth place in the standings.

Today, Monday, a group of essential goods importers held a protest in front of the Ministry of Agriculture Jihad building. The protest was against the failure to fulfill promises and a 19-month delay in paying their foreign currency claims.

The Lebanese army announced that it has discovered and seized more than 260 kilograms of explosives smuggled from Syrian territory in the Bekaa region. The routes for transferring weapons from the Islamic Republic to Hezbollah in Lebanon are becoming increasingly restricted. After the fall of Bashar al-Assad, the route for transferring weapons and explosives from Syria to Lebanon was cut off, and Beirut and Damascus cooperate in pursuing arms smugglers.

The official media of Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, published a threatening design against Jewish identity and religious symbols ahead of the Hanukkah festival. Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel issues, said the Islamic Republic has resorted to old propaganda to mobilize Iranian people who oppose the regime. He added this propaganda is for domestic consumption but has lost its effectiveness because the Iranian people have friendly relations with Israel and its people.

Iranian media reported that Gholamreza Nikkhah, a veteran cinema and television actor, died on Tuesday, 2 Azar, due to a heart attack. Nikkhah was born on 1 Farvardin 1327 and acted in various films and series. He had roles in comedy series and reality shows.

Ahmadreza Radan, the commander of the national police, said at a war-related ceremony that they assure everyone they will identify and suppress any sedition before it starts and will not allow it to emerge. He added that a country known historically for using dirty bombs wants to accuse our country of using these bombs. Radan also said that in the police domain, they have taken the leader's orders as their guiding principle.

Today, Monday, 2 Azar, a number of employees of the Khorasan Razavi Welfare Organization held a protest in front of the Welfare Organization's headquarters in Mashhad, demanding attention to their demands, including the adjustment of their wages and job benefits.

Mohammad Esmaeili Alafi, a lawyer and member of the East Azerbaijan Bar Association, was released from Tabriz prison on Saturday, 30 Aban, after posting a bail of five billion tomans. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

A released video shows that the symbol of the map of Iran installed on the eternal grave of Meysam Abid was destroyed overnight. Meysam Abid was wounded by a gunshot in Fardis on 18 Dey and died in the hospital on 5 Bahman of the same year.

Alireza Mansourian and his Iranian assistants will miss Al-Zawraa's match against Al-Riffa due to Bahrain visa denial. The Iraqi club has requested to move the match to a third country. Al-Zawraa boycotted the pre-match coordination meeting in protest of the visa denial for technical staff members.

The family of Alireza Raeisi was forced by security agents to erase a commemorative poem from his tombstone. Additionally, the tombstone of Meysam Aybed, a 29-year-old killed in the December protests, was destroyed overnight in Malmir village. This information was reported to Iran International.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, responded to Gadi Eisenkot's remarks about the absence of an immediate threat from Iran by saying that the threat from Iran against Israel is immediate. Netanyahu called for the formation of a national unity government including ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties and emphasized the need to reach an agreement with these parties on Israel's Jewish identity and military service.
Today, continuing the gatherings of telecommunications retirees; some of these retirees in the cities of Isfahan and Tehran also held protest gatherings demanding attention to their demands.

The sentences of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi, a singer, and four other members of the "Caravanserai Concert" team named Soheil Faghih Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amir Ali Pirnia, and Mohsen Lashkari were carried out at the enforcement unit of the Qom Prosecutor's Office.

Mostafa Nili, a lawyer, said that the sentence of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi and four of her associates in the historic Dirgachin caravanserai was carried out today, Monday, 2 Azar 1405, at the Qom Prosecutor's Office. According to Nili, these individuals appeared at the enforcement unit of the Qom Prosecutor's Office after the sentence was confirmed by the appeals court, and the lash sentence for all five was executed.

According to Iranian media, the price of the new design coin on Monday, 2 Azar 1405, increased by 13,700,000 tomans to 252 million tomans. The US dollar was also traded at 272,200 tomans in the Iranian market. The price of each gram of 18-carat gold rose from 23,152,100 tomans on Sunday, 1 Azar, to 24,331,700 tomans on Monday.

Players and referees of Serie A teams wore red marks on their faces in the twelfth week matches to show support against violence towards women. The campaign, titled "Red Card to Violence," was held on November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The Serie A football league president said the campaign was a symbol inviting intervention against violence.

David Barnea, former head of Mossad, said that the Israeli intelligence agency, in cooperation with Austrian intelligence agencies, played a key role in thwarting an ISIS plan to attack Taylor Swift's concert in 2024 and prevented the possible death of hundreds. He added that the initial warning came from Austrian partners and Mossad was able to identify the operational network and arrest members of a global jihadist cell. In summer 2024, three Taylor Swift concerts were canceled following security officials' warnings about the ISIS attack plan.

A citizen sent a video showing a restaurant on Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam, where tourists from around the world write graffiti on the walls. The citizen shows a writing by an Iranian that says "Long live Iran, long live the Shah" and the Lion and Sun flag next to the English phrase "Free Iran" on the wall.
Shurush Abubakri, a citizen from Sardasht, was arrested today, Monday, 2 Azar, by the Intelligence Force agents of the IRGC in this city and transferred to an unknown location.

David Barnea, former head of Mossad, called for another war against the Islamic Republic to prevent Tehran from obtaining nuclear weapons and to overthrow the regime at the "Alnet" conference in Jerusalem. He said that a diplomatic agreement with the Islamic Republic will never succeed and that Tehran has pursued its nuclear program for military purposes over the past decades. Barnea emphasized that the Islamic Republic is not willing to convert its nuclear program into a completely civilian one and that obtaining nuclear weapons remains its main goal.

Mostafa Nili, a lawyer, reported the execution of the 74 lashes sentence for Parasto Ahmadi, a singer, and four members of her concert staff. Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, said the Islamic Republic is willing to endure public hatred but continues to scare people because it fears their courage.

The death sentences of three prisoners previously convicted of drug-related crimes and intentional murder were carried out in the prisons of Sabzevar and Qaemshahr. The identities of these prisoners are Ali Nodehi, Afrasiab Emami, and Mohammad Hashemi. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Hamid Bord, acting minister of oil of the Islamic Republic, stated that oil sales are part of the Islamic Republic's tactics in wartime and details are not disclosed to the media. He said oil sales activities continue but the Ministry of Oil does not publicize details. Bord also reported efforts to compensate for lost production in the South Pars gas field and said oil production is stable and gas production is increasing.

Student councils of 31 universities condemned disciplinary cases, suspension orders, and administrative pressures against student representatives in a joint statement. The signatories called for the cancellation of the four-semester suspension of Pejman Nasiri and a review of similar cases. They urged university officials and the Ministry of Science to end retaliatory actions and guarantee the independence and security of student councils and their members' activities.

The ninth week of the Women's Premier Football League continued with victories for Persepolis and Gol Gohar Sirjan and a defeat for Esteghlal. Persepolis defeated Esta Alborz with a single goal by Somayeh Esmaeili and maintained the top of the table. Gol Gohar Sirjan won 5-1 against Malavan, and Esteghlal lost 2-0 to Varesh Nowshahr.

Reuters reported on Monday, quoting five informed sources, that the US is considering a plan to train Syrian army forces in mine clearance and explosive ordnance disposal. The plan, involving several countries including the UK, France, and Saudi Arabia, is under review and may lead to a limited number of US troops returning to Syria next year. The implementation faces legal obstacles in the US and opposition from some Syrian military officials.

The two-semester suspension from studies of Mohammad Mahdi Karimi, an aerospace engineering undergraduate student at Khajeh Nasir University, was confirmed by the university's disciplinary appeals committee.

Media affiliated with the IRGC have justified and promoted the Islamic Republic's missile program by using images of Ferdowsi and Rostam in an animation. Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic exploits Iran's historical and cultural symbols through deception due to a lack of popular and democratic support and increasing gaps between the nation and the government.

Following Bahrain's complaint about the Islamic Republic's attack on its civilian industrial facilities, Islamic Republic broadcasters called Bahrain the "32nd province of Iran." Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said one of the Islamic Republic's goals is to increase tensions with countries it has territorial disputes with. He added that the consequences of these actions will not end even with the fall of the Islamic Republic.

Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, says there is no immediate threat from Iran requiring military action before the formation of Israel's new government, and focus should be on 440 kilograms of enriched uranium from Iran that has not yet been destroyed or removed. Eisenkot made these remarks at his party faction meeting in the Knesset on November 23. In contrast, Benjamin Netanyahu accused his political opponents of downplaying security threats to Israel for political motives and again called for the formation of a unity government.

Bayan Salehian, an internal medicine specialist living in Urmia, was sentenced by the Revolutionary Court of this city to one year in prison and confiscation of electronic devices. He was arrested on 5 Mehr and was released on bail after three weeks of interrogation. This sentence was issued by the third branch of the Revolutionary Court of Urmia on charges of propaganda against the regime.

Benjamin Netanyahu responded to Gadi Eisenkot's statements about the lack of an immediate threat from the Islamic Republic by saying that Iran's threat against Israel is immediate. David Barnea, former head of Mossad, said Israel should attack the Islamic Republic as soon as conditions are ready. These statements were made in an interview with Babak Es-haqi.

Omar Al-Waeli, head of Iraq's Border Crossings Organization, denied on Tuesday, 2 Azar, the closure of the Shalamcheh border crossing between Iran and Iraq, saying the crossing is open and passenger traffic continues normally. Al-Waeli emphasized that the Shalamcheh crossing's activity has not stopped and passenger entry and exit are ongoing without disruption. He added that precise inspections of imported goods are underway but these inspections have not affected the passenger traffic flow.
A video received by Iran International shows a citizen releasing white balloons into the sky in memory of those arrested during the protests in Abdanan on Tuesday, 26 Aban.

According to the monthly report of Aban 1405 by the Statistics Department of the Human Rights Activists in Iran, at least 181 arrests, a total of 6251 months of imprisonment for 49 citizens, 11 trials, and one travel ban were recorded in the field of freedom of thought and expression during this month. Additionally, 11 summonses to judicial authorities, a fine of 1.68 billion tomans, 11 executions of prison sentences, 4 cases of asset confiscation, and 11 house searches were reported.

At the start of the fifth week of the Asian Elite Football League, Esteghlal is a guest of Al Ain in the UAE and Tractor hosts Al Wasl in Oman. This news was reported with an assessment by Mohammad Taghavi, Iran International.
Shokrallah Ahmadi, a teachers' union activist, was reportedly arrested yesterday by national security police forces in Nurabad Mamasani and transferred to the Soroush detention center in Shiraz.
Heyman Khorshidi, a citizen from Baneh, was sentenced to two years and three months of imprisonment by the Revolutionary Court of that city.

Published images show that the players of the Varash Nowshahr women's team celebrated after defeating Esteghlal in the ninth week of the Women's Premier League. Varash defeated Esteghlal 2-0 and reached 12 points. Varash is sixth with one game less, and Esteghlal is fourth with 16 points.

Kuwait's official news agency, KUNA, reported that the Council of Ministers of Kuwait strongly condemned the repeated attacks by Iran on Kuwaiti territory, including last Wednesday's drone attack. The Council described these attacks as a clear violation of Kuwait's sovereignty and a direct threat to the country's security and stability. The Kuwaiti government also stated that these attacks constitute a serious violation of international law, the United Nations Charter, and the UN Security Council resolution.

Reuters reported that Russia's attempt to return to international sports competitions after the lifting of its suspension by the International Olympic Committee has faced widespread opposition from European countries. Norway, Sweden, and Poland have refused to issue visas to Russian athletes, and some national teams are unwilling to compete against Russia. The dispute over the participation of Russian athletes may affect the qualifying competitions for the 2028 Olympics.

A prisoner in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj, previously sentenced to death for murder, was transferred to solitary confinement on Monday, 2 Azar, for the execution of his death sentence. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Kazem Gharibabadi, Deputy of the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, requested the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons to examine the consequences of US and Israeli attacks on facilities under its inspection in Iran. He stated that some declared Iranian facilities were damaged and called for a clear stance from the organization and an investigation into the technical, human, and environmental aspects of these attacks.

Hormozgan University of Medical Sciences reported the death of three people due to alcohol poisoning in Bandar Abbas and the hospitalization of 13 people in the province. The number of alcohol poisoning cases in Nishapur reached 191. At least eight people have died from alcohol poisoning recently in Hormozgan, Khorasan Razavi, and Fars.

Esteghlal football team drew 1-1 with Al Ain in the fifth week of the Asian Elite League in the UAE. The goals were scored by Saman Fallah in the 51st minute for Esteghlal and Palacios in the 69th minute for Al Ain. Esteghlal reached 10 points and moved to third place in the West Asia table, while Al Ain remains the leader with 13 points.

Nejat Bahrami, a political analyst, said the Trump administration seeks the gradual weakening of the Islamic Republic and pushing it toward collapse, but Israel wants a faster military action. He added there is a possibility of adding a military option to the economic pressures against the Islamic Republic.

Prince Reza Pahlavi's media office stated on X that the Islamic Republic fears women's voices and described the flogging of Parasto Ahmadi and four others involved in the Caravanserai concert as a "brutal" act aimed at humiliating and suppressing artists. The office called the concert a lasting symbol of women's resistance against the Islamic Republic's restrictions and emphasized that women's voices in Iran cannot be censored. It also criticized the Islamic Republic's treatment of artists, referring to the role of art and music before the 1979 revolution, and expressed hope that women in Iran will freely participate in artistic, social, economic, and political fields in the future.

Tractor football team lost heavily 5-1 to Al Wasl UAE in the fifth week of the Asian Elite League. Mehdi Taremi scored two goals and provided one assist. Mohammad Daneshgar was sent off in the 18th minute and Tractor goalkeeper Parsa Jafari was taken off the field late in the game.
An audio version of Titraval with Niusha Saremi discusses the escalation of maritime confrontation between Tehran and Washington and calls for a new war in Israel.

Videos published on social media show smoke rising from a ship near the coast of Oman. Satellite images from Tuesday, 2 Azar also show smoke rising from a ship in the same location. The flag or ownership details of this ship and the exact date of the videos have not been independently verified.
Five workers died and four others were injured in work accidents in six cities: Masal, Saveh, Bukan, Urmia, Tehran, and Arak.

Iran says it will not tolerate continued US sanctions and blockade and will use all tools at its disposal to counter them. Donald Trump, US president, threatened in an interview with Fox News that he would sink Iranian ships if Iran attempts to break the naval blockade. The conversation was with Farzin Nadimi, senior defense and security researcher at the Washington Institute.

Health officials in Fars province reported about 30 alcohol poisoning cases and one death in Shiraz and Marvdasht. The number of alcohol poisoning cases in Nishapur has increased to 120, with four deaths. Homemade and counterfeit alcoholic drinks are main causes, and some citizens criticize the alcohol ban as a factor in expanding the black market and increasing poisoning risks.

According to the United States Geological Survey, in the early hours of Monday, November 23, the summit of Kilauea volcano in Hawaii erupted, with lava reaching up to 200 meters above the ground. The lava ejection started at 12:15 AM local time and continued until 6 AM. This was the fifty-seventh eruption phase of Kilauea since December 23, 2024.
A man accused of killing his wife and daughter in the Chitgar area of Tehran was sentenced to death by Branch 10 of the Tehran Provincial Criminal Court.

The Islamic Republic faces a series of simultaneous crises, each of which could seriously challenge a government. These crises include the risk of a new war with the US and Israel, an oil blockade, leadership crisis, governance split, unprecedented inflation, rising bread prices, and shortages of water, electricity, and gas. There is no sign of these crises abating, and each can exacerbate the others.

About 400 faculty members of Farhangian University were forcibly retired contrary to a previous board resolution and face deductions in seniority bases and 16 months of unpaid wages. A contract worker in South Pars reported incomplete payment of wage claims, ambiguity in salary and benefits calculation, and his dismissal. Additionally, six workers of Navid Babakan Company in Shahrbabak were dismissed during a one-week workers' strike.

A citizen from Maragheh sent a video to Iran International, sarcastically responding to Ali Khamenei's statements about the power outage, saying: "We have reached the peak, but here there is neither water, gas, nor electricity."

Kezhal Mobaraki and Jamal Ahmadzadeh, two researchers and a couple living in Urmia, remain in detention nearly five months after their arrest. Their case is being processed in the second branch of the Urmia Revolutionary Court.

Akbar Moradi, the Tractor doctor, said about Parsa Jafari's injury that at the 3rd minute of the game, a hit to his neck occurred but there was no significant injury. In the final minutes of the game, Jafari lost consciousness and then regained it, and was sent to the hospital for MRI and CT scan. Moradi said he is optimistic about Jafari's recovery and they will monitor him until his return to Iran.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, said the Islamic Republic has triumphed over the enemy in military and diplomatic fields, and both diplomacy and war are tools to achieve deterrent power. He added that diplomacy alone cannot remove the shadow of war from the country, and fighting alone cannot eliminate this threat. Ghalibaf also said the aerospace industry of the Islamic Republic has placed Iran among the top four powers in this field.
Iran International reported that the audio version of Cheshmandaz contains statements advocating turning away from Khomeini's explicit principles to preserve the regime.

About 9 months after the announcement of the third leader of the regime, a video of the Assembly of Experts' session on the voting day was released. The Friday prayer leader of Najafabad revealed that the experts' representatives had previously written his name individually, but the session was held so that it would not be perceived that Mojtaba Khamenei was chosen by the IRGC. A report by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.
Former Mossad chief said that military action must be taken immediately to overthrow the Islamic Republic.
A video received by Iran International shows that protesters in Haft-Juy village in Tehran province have installed a banner supporting Abdanan on a pedestrian bridge.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the Prime Minister of Qatar, said Doha is working with the Islamic Republic and the United States to revive the negotiation process. He added that the Middle East cannot tolerate new escalations of tension between the US and Iran. He also stated that the strategic dialogue with the US is a fundamental pillar of their relations and they seek to strengthen cooperation in defense sectors.

While Israel pressures to resume military attacks on the Islamic Republic and mediators try to reach an agreement between Tehran and Washington, mutual threats and military positions have increased uncertainty about the future of tensions. Officials of the Islamic Republic speak of unlimited geographical response, which could indicate an expansion of the regime's threats in case of a new conflict.

Ahmad Alavi, a university professor and economist, said that alternative land, rail, and Caspian Sea routes cannot replace the Persian Gulf trade routes in terms of cost or effectiveness. He added that activating these routes is mostly symbolic and has not prevented the shrinking economy and contraction of Iran's foreign trade.

The sentence of 74 lashes was carried out for Parasto Ahmadi and four members of her group due to performing a concert without mandatory hijab in Qom. These five artists were also sentenced to two years of travel ban and prohibition from artistic activities.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the debate over a renewed attack on the Islamic Republic has heated up in Israel. Eisenkot, tasked with forming the new Israeli government, says there is currently no need for an immediate attack. However, Netanyahu warns that the threat from the Islamic Republic is serious and those downplaying it have political motives.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Dovi Barnea, former head of Mossad, has called for a swift and decisive attack on the Islamic Republic aimed at overthrowing it. He said the economic consequences of war must be accepted and warned European countries that the continuation of the Islamic Republic means maintaining the motivation to acquire nuclear weapons and poses a threat to Israel's existence and European security.

Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has been reappointed as the CEO of the company. The Nvidia board unanimously agreed to his return after several rounds of talks with Huang. Harvey Jones, chairman of the board, said senior US government officials participated in the decision and concluded that Huang's return does not pose a national security threat.

Axios and The Times of Israel reported that Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, met with JD Vance, Trump's deputy, in Washington and discussed efforts to reach a diplomatic solution aimed at ending the conflict between the US and the Islamic Republic. A source familiar with The Times of Israel said the meeting lasted about 10 minutes and the main purpose of the Qatari delegation's trip was to participate in the annual strategic talks between the US and Qatar with the presence of Marco Rubio. Al Thani also met with Rubio before meeting Vance.

According to Mostafa Nili, a lawyer, the sentence of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi and four members of her group in the "Caravanserai Concert" case has been carried out. The concert was hypothetical, but the lashes were real. A program will discuss human dignity and ways to end flogging punishment.

Sohrab Bakhtiyari-Zadeh, Esteghlal's head coach, said after a draw with Al Ain UAE in the fifth week of the Asian Elite League that they could have won the game and that their goalkeeper and defensive structure worked very well. He added that his players were outstanding and that their team is a great team. Bakhtiyari-Zadeh also said that Al Ain is a high-quality and powerful team but Esteghlal is also a quality and strong team, and playing in Al Ain's home stadium is very difficult.

Mostafa Nili, the lawyer of Parasto Ahmadi, announced that this singer and four members of the "Concert Caravanserai" group each received 74 lashes at the Qom Prosecutor's Office. This sentence was issued following the release of a "virtual concert" video of Parasto Ahmadi singing without mandatory hijab at the historic Dirgachin Caravanserai. Branch 122 of the Qom Criminal Court convicted these five individuals of "pretending to commit an immoral act" and Branch 16 of the Qom Court of Appeals confirmed the sentence.

Alireza Beiranvand, Tractor's goalkeeper, said that his three-year contract extension with Tractor happened in less than 30 minutes without the presence of Hojat Karimi, the club's CEO. He added that Karimi was not present in the negotiations and he pursued the contract signing from Karimi for several days, but the club did not send him the signed contract. Beiranvand also stated that he wrote to the league organization that Hojat Karimi did not sign his contract before resigning, and therefore he has no contract with the club.

Officials of the Islamic Republic emphasized resistance against external pressures, considered the land blockade of Iran impossible, and spoke of victories in military and diplomatic fields and efforts to break the blockade.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said that the sanctions on Iran's currency and gold exchange center and several exchange offices target the conversion of export currency into financial resources needed for imports. He emphasized that the pressure of sanctions and limitations on oil revenues have severely reduced the Islamic Republic's ability to finance proxy groups.

The South Korean military announced that several Russian fighters briefly entered its air defense identification zone over the East Sea early Tuesday. The South Korean Air Force scrambled fighters in response, and the Russian planes left without violating South Korean airspace. The South Korean Ministry of Defense said it will summon the Russian military attaché to protest the air defense identification zone breach.

The Guardian reported, citing documents obtained by Ukrainian hackers and Belarusian opposition hackers, that over 460,000 war-related deaths have been recorded in Russia since the start of the Ukraine war. Last year, the war became the leading cause of death for Russian men under 65. 2025 was the deadliest year of the war, with an average of 548 men dying daily.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Prime Minister of Qatar, after meeting with the US Secretary of State, said his country continues efforts to reduce tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US and revive negotiations. He added that Qatar has been working in recent months to revive negotiations and the diplomatic path and is in continuous contact with both countries. Al Thani called on both sides to reduce tensions and create conditions for diplomacy.

Nikki Haley, former US ambassador to the UN, called on the Trump administration to target the shadow banking network in China and Hong Kong to block the last financial routes of the Islamic Republic and end the war. She said the issue is not sending more ground troops or bombing but cutting off the flow of money and oil. Haley added that cutting financial resources would prevent the Islamic Republic from funding proxy groups and building missiles.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations instructor, said the United States is ready to cooperate with the Syrian army at various levels, from training and information exchange to institution-building and strengthening command structures. He said Washington is shaping a new security architecture in the region, and Arab countries are seeking to establish a security order without the presence of the Islamic Republic.

Hundreds of schools in Germany and Denmark have faced a new wave of bomb threats, with senders demanding the overthrow of the government and the implementation of Islamic Sharia law. German police have stated that so far no evidence of involvement by Islamist groups has been found. Jalal Ejadi, a sociology professor, explained the impact of these threats on public trust and political divides in Europe from a political sociology perspective.

Forced retirement of about 400 faculty members at Farhangian University has faced protests from the university's professors. These professors have reported deductions in their seniority bases and up to 16 months of uncertainty in receiving their salaries. Rouzbeh Boulehri explains the goals of dismissing protesting workers and the impact of these actions on workers' protests.

The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. officials are investigating the possibility of the Islamic Republic's involvement in cyberattacks on about 50 commercial ships carrying oil, liquefied gas, and hazardous materials.

Results of a new clinical trial show that a skin cancer-specific vaccine, jointly produced by Moderna and Merck, combined with immunotherapy has reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death from it by 42 percent. These results have increased hopes for the use of personalized vaccines in cancer treatment.

Representatives of the International Center for Human Rights and the Silent Conscripts Support Network met with Canadian government officials to request the removal of immigration restrictions against Iranians who have completed their mandatory military service in the IRGC. Ardshir Zarezadeh, a lawyer and human rights activist, explains the proposals made in this meeting and the Canadian officials' reactions.

Simultaneous with Qatar's efforts to revive negotiations between the Islamic Republic and the United States, Tehran's disputes with regional countries and reactions to the joint statement by Qatar and Germany continue. Officials of the Islamic Republic have reported ongoing contacts with mediators and emphasized expanding economic cooperation with neighboring countries.

The former commander of the British Navy claimed that the Islamic Republic's allegations about mine-laying in the Strait of Hormuz are part of the government's psychological warfare. He wrote that none of the three reputable maritime organizations have confirmed the IRGC's reports about ships hitting naval mines.

Abbas Golrou, head of the International Relations Committee of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Parliament, stated that if another war occurs, "the world must say goodbye to oil." He added that the Islamic Republic has tools and capacities that can influence regional and global equations. Golrou also said that the military and defense capabilities of the Islamic Republic are developing and that naval blockade and economic pressures will be neutralized by the initiative of officials.

Alaeddin Boroujerdi, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that entering the new phase of deterrence in the Islamic Republic has many supporters and that it is necessary to reach sustainable deterrence. He said that the Islamic Republic cannot tolerate economic blockade and recently warned it would send its tankers. He added that if the Americans prevent this, it would mean a return to wartime conditions and other actions will be taken.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, announced that no action or negotiation will take place before the implementation of the seven conditions of the Islamic Republic. He referred to recent remarks by Donald Trump and the US Treasury Secretary and said the Islamic Republic's position is clear and unchangeable. Ghalibaf also stated that they are ready to respond decisively to enemy movements.

Rouhollah Rahimpour, a journalist and political analyst, said that Qalibaf defines the victory of the Islamic Republic mainly by the survival of the government; while the real criterion of victory should be the improvement of security, welfare, and freedom of the Iranian people.

The annual meeting of the International Network of Nuclear Security Training and Support Centers began on Monday, 2 Azar, in Islamabad. In this four-day conference, about 68 representatives from 49 countries have gathered to strengthen international cooperation in nuclear security.

BBC Sport has reported that Gianni Infantino has made 39 private jet flights in the past 115 days. He has traveled to 32 countries since late July and covered over 102,000 air miles. These trips were made with private jets from Qatar Executive, but FIFA has not clarified the costs involved.

A mother of a student shows bruises on her child's body in a video and says the principal of Moftah School in Aligudarz, Lorestan province, severely beat her child with a hose because the child did not know the lesson.

Mojtaba Khamenei wrote in a message to the "National Youth Population Award event" that every proud Iranian who desires a bright future has a strong motivation to continue the Iranian generation in line with the new Islamic civilization. He added that he hopes Iran will safely pass through the critical and decisive stage by compensating for past population policy shortcomings and pursuing the correct strategy of increasing the young population and focusing on the family.

Japan Times reported that North Korean intelligence agents, disguised as a sports delegation, had an unofficial contact with Japanese officials during the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The Japanese representative proposed that if Pyongyang showed flexibility on the issue of Japanese citizens abducted decades ago, North Korea would benefit from normalized bilateral relations. However, North Korea insisted that no talks about the abductees would occur before resolving the "comfort women" issue and historical war settlements, and left the meeting.

Eight Sunni citizens of Ahvaz were released from Sheiban prison on bail of 10 billion tomans. Jafar Cheldavi, Abbas Heydari, Mostafa Cheldavi, Loghman Batran, Hadi Beit Sheikh Ahmad, Amir Jaderi, Reza Savari, and Milad Khalasizadeh were released from prison. Khaled Gharbavi and Jasim Tuwirat remain in detention and in a state of judicial uncertainty.
